canonical.title: Check If an Inorder Sequence Can Belong to a BST
canonical.sourceFilePath: 12. Binary Search Trees/1. Concept/01. Intro to BST.cpp

narrative.title: The Ledger Sequence Sanity Check
narrative.scenario: A records desk receives a day's transactions already sorted by a walk that always visits smaller amounts before larger ones. Before the batch is filed, a clerk runs one sanity check: a walk with that property must never show an amount that fails to rise against the one before it. One flat scan settles whether the sequence could have come from such a filing tree at all.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer array order — a claimed inorder traversal of a binary search tree.
narrative.outputFormat: Return true if the sequence is strictly increasing (a valid BST inorder), otherwise false.

testCases.explanation: Every entry rises over its predecessor, so the walk is consistent with a BST.
The 3-to-2 drop breaks the non-decreasing guarantee of any BST inorder.

hintLevels: Level 1: A BST read left-to-right is a sorted reading — just prove the reading never dips.
Level 2: Compare each element only with its immediate predecessor; no tree needs to be built.
Level 3: Insist on strict increase — an equal neighbour is already a contradiction.
